title: The System That Models Itself
case: Daylight-saving transitions and fatal road crashes
claim_tested: Disrupting a maintenance schedule can impair subsequent regulated performance.
design: Within-year difference-in-differences comparing mean daily fatal crashes in weeks -2/-1 and +1/+2 in DST and non-DST states, omitting transition day.
identification_limits: Clock changes alter daylight as well as sleep; crashes do not directly measure maintenance or cognition
This adapter gives yearly point contrasts, not a replication of Smith's richer design
Does not identify self-modeling, consciousness, or the complete autopoietic loop
Indiana excluded throughout; Arizona excludes counties 001, 005, 017 and unknown county codes; controls remain geographically different
Unknown-date crashes are not imputed; compatible-date accounting bounds are not confidence intervals
Raw crash counts are not adjusted for miles driven or population; only two non-DST comparison units

result.conclusion: Schedule/performance component comparison; daylight, travel, weather, and sleep mechanisms are not separated. The earlier-window placebo is larger in absolute magnitude than the event contrast, weakening a clean causal interpretation.

metadata.construction: Complete national ACCIDENT.csv records, 2000–2015, one row per fatal crash. Count by fixed geography and date; complete the calendar with zeros for known-date records. Retain unknown-day/month records separately without date imputation; bound their possible effect on window contrasts. Reject invalid known dates, missing identifiers, duplicate crashes, or absent states. No crash microdata are committed.
metadata.coverage: 2000–2015; 48 DST geographic units and two non-DST controls: Hawaii and Arizona excluding counties 001, 005, 017, plus county unknown codes 000/999. Exclude Indiana in every year. Arizona is a partial-state aggregate, not a full-state estimate.
metadata.assignment: Spring DST transition by applicable US rule (first Sunday in April through 2006, second Sunday in March thereafter). Geography is classified by policy, not by outcomes. No random assignment; seasonal travel, weather, daylight, and control comparability remain threats.
metadata.units: Fatal crashes per geographic unit per local calendar day; not fatalities, rates per mile, or individual cognitive measurements.
